name: Classic bass-swap transition
lesson:
## The transition every DJ is judged on

Deck B starts with its bass fully cut (the low knob turned off before you press play). Bring B in over the first 8 bars on hi and mids only, so two kicks never fight. At bar 17, swap the bass over 4 bars: A's low down while B's low comes up to centre. Then A's fader out over bars 25 to 33.

The reason it works: two bass lines in the same register cancel and mud the mix; the swap means exactly one kick owns the low end at every moment.

tracks.cue: The M1 organ bass is the whole track. A plays from the verse; at bar 17 its low knob comes down over 4 bars and the room hears exactly one bassline the whole time.
Cue B at its first kick with the low knob off. Bring it in on hi and mid; its bassline hook arrives on a phrase line, so time the swap so B's low is at centre when the hook lands.
Alternative B: the filtered loop rides on a bass that never stops, so any moment both lows are up is audible mud. Good for hearing why the swap has to be clean.
